summary: Rust repository-topology analyzer built from the `native/repograph` crate that ships in the charness checkout. Use when a gate needs export-safety, plugin-reference, standalone-target, or path-classification facts derived from real Python ASTs instead of regex approximations.

commands: if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'repograph: cargo is required to build this binary. Install Rust from https://rustup.rs then re-run `charness tool install repograph`.' >&2; exit 1; fi; crate=''; for candidate in "$PWD/native/repograph" "${CHARNESS_SRC:-$HOME/.agents/src/charness}/native/repograph"; do if [ -f "$candidate/Cargo.toml" ]; then crate="$candidate"; break; fi; done; if [ -z "$crate" ]; then echo 'repograph: no charness checkout carrying native/repograph was found in this repo or at ${CHARNESS_SRC:-$HOME/.agents/src/charness}. Run `charness update` to obtain the managed checkout, then re-run this install.' >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "repograph: building from $crate"; cd "$crate" && cargo install --path . --locked --force
notes: The binary is BUILT from the crate that ships in the charness checkout, not downloaded. That is deliberate: building from the checkout that runs the gates makes version skew between binary and source structurally impossible instead of detecting it after the fact.

The install command must `cd` into the crate directory before `cargo install --path .`. Rustup selects the toolchain from the working directory, so installing from elsewhere ignores `native/repograph/rust-toolchain.toml` and fails against the crate's pinned `rust-version`.
`--force` is required because the crate version does not bump per commit; without it cargo refuses every reinstall as already-present and the binary silently stays at the previous commit's behavior.
`--locked` is required because `Cargo.lock` ships with the crate and a blocking gate verdict must not vary with dependency resolution drift.
`cargo install` writes to `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin`. If that directory is not on PATH for the current process, add it (`export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"`) or start a new shell.

Update means rebuild from the current checkout: run `charness update` first so the crate source matches the charness version you intend to run, then `charness tool install repograph`. Install IS the update path here; there is no separate upgrade command.
A rebuild is only needed when `native/repograph/**` changed. When the crate is unchanged, the installed binary is already the matching commit's binary.

Deliberately `manual` rather than `script`: `docs/control-plane.md` limits script-mode updates to a single canonical command that does not inspect PATH, and the rebuild's own precondition check would violate that. The install lifecycle owns the branch instead.

detect.failure_hint: Build and install `repograph` with `charness tool install repograph`; the export-safety and plugin-reference gates have no fallback path and fail closed without it.

healthcheck.failure_hint: The `repograph` binary exists but did not emit its machine-readable export-safe report. Rebuild it with `charness tool install repograph` against the current checkout.

version_expectation.constraint: The binary must be built from the `native/repograph` crate of the charness checkout whose gates consume it. There is no independent upstream version to pin; the crate has no `--version` flag by design, because its identity is the checkout commit it was built from.

when_missing: `check-export-safe-imports` and `check-plugin-dir-references` are BLOCKING quality gates with no fallback engine; a missing `repograph` makes them fail closed rather than pass silently.
`check_standalone_imports.py` cannot enumerate standalone targets, so the consumer-repo standalone-import contract is unproven, not satisfied.
Do not substitute a regex or `splitlines()` approximation for any of the above. The gates exist because AST-derived facts and text approximations disagree.
when_version_mismatch: A binary built from a different commit than the checkout under analysis is a version mismatch even though nothing reports one. Rebuild with `charness tool install repograph` after any change under `native/repograph/**`.

host_notes: No `package_managers` block on purpose, even though the binary is installed by cargo. `install_provenance_lib.package_manager_update_action` turns `package_managers.cargo.package_name` into `cargo install <name> --force`, which resolves against crates.io. `repograph` is not published there, so that derived command would reach for an unrelated crate of the same name. Declaring the block and adding a note saying `must not be installed by name` would not help: nothing reads the note, and the derivation reads the block.

This is the only repo-provided tool in the control plane: its upstream repository IS charness, and its source ships in the same checkout that consumes it. It replaced a prebuilt-artifact distribution layer (download, checksum, staging, atomic activation, version pruning, rollback) that existed solely to deliver this one binary; building from the present source makes the skew states that layer detected impossible rather than detectable.

`detect` and `healthcheck` both fall back to `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin` so that `charness tool install repograph` followed immediately by `charness tool doctor repograph` agrees in a process whose PATH predates the cargo install. `scripts/native_gate_lib.py` applies the same two-step lookup, so the doctor verdict and the gate resolution can never disagree about whether the binary is reachable.

The two checks express that fallback differently on purpose. `detect` must START with the bare binary name, because `install_provenance_lib.detect_binary_name` derives `provenance.binary_name` from `shlex.split(checks.detect.commands[0])[0]`; a `PATH=... repograph` prefix there reports `PATH=...` as the binary name in the doctor payload. `healthcheck` is not read that way and uses the plainer PATH prefix, which also avoids re-running the probe when `export-safe` exits non-zero on a repo that has violations.

The upstream release probe reports charness's own latest GitHub release, because `upstream_repo` is this repository. That is accurate but is NOT an install source: `asset_names` is empty and always will be. The `next_step` text states the build-from-source path explicitly so the release line cannot be read as something to download.

Gate resolution order is `CHARNESS_NATIVE_CORE` override, then `<repo-root>/native/repograph/target/release/repograph` when the crate is present (the charness authoring checkout), then the installed binary. Dev-tree precedes the installed binary so an edited crate is reflected in the gate verdict instead of being answered by a binary built from other source.

Only linux is exercised by this repo's own gate runs today. macos and windows are declared because the install path is a host build rather than a per-tuple prebuilt artifact, which is what made the previous layer's platform-tuple table a maintenance surface.
